paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The people asked, "Where is the God of justice?" and the LORD answered with a promise: "Behold, I will send My messenger, who will prepare the way before Me." (Malachi 3:1) He didn't say justice was missing. He said He was coming. The question was never whether He sees, it was whether they were ready to be seen.

And listen, this is where it gets real. They wanted the Lord to show up, but the passage asks, "But who can endure the day of His coming?" (Malachi 3:2) His answer is that He will be "like a refiner's fire, like a launderer's soap." A refiner doesn't heat silver to wreck it. He sits there and watches until the good comes through, and then "the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will please the LORD, as in days of old and years gone by." (Malachi 3:3-4) I know a little about being worn down and made new, and I'm telling you, that kind of cleaning is a gift.

So what do you do with it, baker? You stop asking Him to hurry up on everybody else's cookies and let Him work on yours. The LORD names real sins, like cheating workers of their wages and denying justice to the foreigner, and He says they come from people who "do not fear Me." (Malachi 3:5) Fear Him, let Him refine you, and keep your oven ready. This is one of the prophets pointing ahead, and the story of what's coming isn't over.
